info.title: Awrad API
info.summary: JSON API served by awrad-server-next to the Android, iOS and web clients.
info.description:
Follows `contracts/api/STYLE.md` (ADR-2026-10-16). Rules are enforced by
`contracts/api/spectral.mjs`; run `npm test` in `contracts/`.

Paths are added slice by slice (`docs/rebuild-plan.md`). Shared building
blocks live under `components` and are referenced, never copied.

servers.description: The deployment's API origin. Web clients use their own origin (same site).

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: Registration, email verification, password reset and the signed-in account (slice 2a).

tags.name: device_sessions
tags.description: Mobile sign-in, token refresh and sign-out (ADR-2026-07-12).

tags.name: account_settings
tags.description: Sessions, password, email and deletion for the signed-in account (slice 2b).

tags.name: sync
tags.description: The change queue: commands and the changes feed for custom dhikrs, tags and personal records (slice 3b, contracts/sync/v1).

tags.name: audio
tags.description: Private recordings for custom dhikrs: reserve an upload, PUT the file straight to storage, confirm it, then fetch short-lived download links (slice 3c, contracts/audio/v1, ADR-2026-10-29).

post.summary: Create an account and email a verification code
post.description: Verification-first (ADR-2026-07-12): the account can't sign in until its email is verified with `verify_account_email`. Always `202`, also when the email already has an account, so the response doesn't reveal it. A new code cancels any earlier one.

post.summary: Verify an account's email with the emailed code
post.description: Marks the email verified. It doesn't sign in: the client then calls `create_device_session` (mobile) or `create_browser_session` (web) with the password it already has. A wrong, expired or used code, or an unknown email, is `verification_code_invalid`. After 5 wrong tries the code is spent.
Always `202`. Sent only to an account that exists and isn't verified yet; the new code cancels the old one.
Always `202`. Sent only when the email has an account; a new code cancels the old one.

post.summary: Set a new password with the emailed reset code
post.description: Sets the password and **revokes every session of the account**, mobile and browser. The code also proves the inbox, so an unverified email becomes verified. A wrong, expired or used code, or an unknown email, is `reset_code_invalid`; after 5 wrong tries the code is spent. The client then signs in with the new password.

422.description: `reset_code_invalid`, or `validation_failed` with field codes `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common` on `/new_password`.

example.title: Reset code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

get.description: Accepts either credential; each pipeline checks only its own (ADR-2026-10-15).

get.summary: Every place the account is signed in
get.description: Mobile device sessions and browser sessions together, most recently used first, with the caller's own marked `is_current`. Only active sessions are listed. An account rarely has more than a page.

delete.summary: Sign out one device or browser
delete.description: Ends that session; its next request is `401`. Revoking the caller's own session is the same as signing out. Another account's session, one already ended, or an id that isn't a UUID is `404`.

post.summary: Sign out of all other devices and browsers
post.description: Ends every session of the account except the caller's own.

post.summary: Change the password while signed in
post.description: Needs the current password. Signs out every other device and browser and keeps the caller signed in. The account's email gets a notice that the password changed.

Needs the current password. Emails a 6-digit code to the NEW address; nothing changes until `confirm_email_change`. Always `202` for a valid request: if the new address already belongs to another account, that address gets a notice instead of a code, so the response doesn't reveal it. A new request cancels the previous code.

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: new_email is the account's current email

post.summary: Confirm the new email with the code sent to it
post.description: Switches the account to the new address and returns the account. The old address gets a notice of the change. Sessions stay signed in. A wrong, expired or used code is `email_change_code_invalid` (5 tries). If the new address was taken by another account in the meantime, `409 email_taken`.

200.description: The account with its new email.

409.description: The new address now belongs to another account.

example.title: Email taken
example.detail: the new email now belongs to another account

example.title: Email change code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

post.description: Needs the current password. Immediately and permanently deletes the account and everything the server keeps for it (sessions, settings, synced data), and ends every session; a browser's cookies are cleared. Practice data stored on devices isn't touched: the apps keep working offline. The address gets a confirmation email. There is no undo. A retry after a lost `204` gets `401`, because the account no longer exists: clients treat `401` after a delete request as done.

post.summary: Sign in on a mobile device
post.description: Creates a device session and returns its tokens. Signing in again from the same installation replaces that installation's session. If the password is right but the email isn't verified, the response is `403 email_verification_required` and the server emails a fresh code (rate-limited), so the client can go straight to the code screen.

password.description: Not checked against the password rules here; a wrong one is `invalid_credentials`.

422.description: `validation_failed`. Field codes: `email_invalid` on `/email`; `installation_id_invalid`, `device_name_invalid` or `platform_invalid` under `/device/...` (an app bug, not something a person can fix).

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: device.platform is not supported

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and get a new access token
post.description: Each refresh token works once. `Idempotency-Key` is **required** here: a retry with the same key within 60 seconds returns the same new tokens, so a lost response doesn't sign the device out. Reusing a spent token any other way is `refresh_reuse_detected` and revokes the session. Clients run at most one refresh at a time, keep their tokens on network errors, and drop them only on `401`.

401.description: `refresh_token_invalid` (unknown, expired, or its session ended), `refresh_reuse_detected` (the session is now revoked) or `account_deleted` (the token belonged to an account that no longer exists; only the holder of a once-valid refresh token learns this, so it reveals nothing to others). Either way the device is signed out. On `account_deleted` a phone offers to remove that account's local profile (contracts/sync/v1, `profile_switch`).

example.title: Refresh token invalid
example.detail: the refresh token is unknown or its session has ended

post.description: Revokes the session that owns the refresh token. It takes the refresh token rather than the access token, so it works after an app restart when no access token is held. Always `204`, also for an unknown or already revoked token, so clients can retry it until it succeeds.

get.summary: Get the CSRF token for this browser session
get.description: Works for any browser, signed in or not (ADR-2026-10-15). When the browser has no session cookie yet, this call creates the anonymous session and sets its cookie, so a signed-out browser can then call `create_browser_session`. The web app sends the returned token in `X-CSRF-Token` on every state-changing request. Only the session cookie is read here; a bearer token is ignored.

200.description: The session's CSRF token. Sets the session cookie if there wasn't one.

post.description: Sets the Phoenix session cookie (and the remember-me cookie when `remember_me` is true). Needs the session cookie and CSRF token that `get_browser_csrf_token` gives any browser. Signing in renews the session, so the response carries the new CSRF token. An unverified email gets `403 email_verification_required`, and the server emails a fresh code (rate-limited). A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` signs in again rather than replaying, because a stored response can't set the cookie (STYLE §10).

remember_me.description: Keep the browser signed in for 14 days (sliding). Defaults to true.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

delete.description: Deletes the session and remember-me cookies and the server-side session token.

post.description:
Applies 1 to 100 commands in order and returns one receipt per command, in the same order. A command's outcome never undoes the others. The account's batches are serialized; every applied command takes the next revision.

**Batch versus command problems.** The batch is refused as a whole (`422 validation_failed`, nothing applied) only when it has 0 or more than 100 commands, or a command's envelope is wrong: `command_id` or `entity_id` not a UUID, an unknown `entity_type` or `op`, `base_version` not an integer in range, `document` missing on a put, present on a delete or not an object, or an unknown member (sync.schema.json `command_envelope`). Everything else is a per-command `rejected` receipt, including a document that doesn't match its schema below: the server checks each document itself, so one bad command never blocks a phone's queue.

Receipts: `applied` (`version`, `revision`, and `cascaded`: for a `user_tag` or `custom_dhikr` delete, every other entity the server changed at the same revision, whose known versions phones update straight away; null for other commands), `duplicate` (same `command_id` and payload as before; carries the original receipt), `conflict` (stale `base_version`; carries the server's copy), `merged` (a tag create whose name an active tag already has; the new ID becomes an alias), `gone` (the entity is deleted, or is a merged tag ID) and `rejected` (`code`, `fields`, and the server's copy or null; `audio_not_found` when a custom dhikr names an audio asset that isn't a ready asset of the account, `audio_mismatch` when its size or type isn't the asset's, contracts/audio/v1; `entity_id_invalid` when a `practice_policy` or `goal_order` entity_id isn't the account's ID; `delete_not_allowed` for a `dhikr_personal`, `practice_policy` or `goal_order` delete; `dhikr_not_found` when a goal names neither a built-in dhikr nor a custom dhikr of the account; `goal_limit_reached` past 300 goals that haven't ended or 2,000 in all; `goal_field_immutable` when a put changes a stored goal's `dhikr_id` or `counts`, with an `immutable` error on each). Receipts are kept for 90 days.

**Goals (slice 4).** A goal is one whole document (contracts/goal-model/v1); a put that breaks the goal rules is `rejected` with `document_invalid`. Deleting a custom dhikr ends each of its goals that hasn't ended (`ended.reason: dhikr_deleted`) at the same revision, listed in `cascaded`; a goal put naming an already deleted custom dhikr is applied and stored ended. A `goal_order` keeps only the account's non-deleted goals.

`Idempotency-Key` isn't needed: each command is idempotent by its `command_id` (STYLE §10). The server accepts the header and ignores it. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.description: Accepted and ignored; commands are idempotent by command_id.

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

200.description: One receipt per command, in order, and the account's head revision after the batch.

422.description: `validation_failed`: the batch is malformed, and nothing was applied. Field codes: `batch_size_invalid` on `/commands` (0 or more than 100 commands); `command_malformed` on `/commands/{i}` or a member of it (the command's envelope is wrong). Problems inside a document are `rejected` receipts, never this.

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: a batch holds 1 to 100 commands

get.summary: Read the account's changes after a revision
get.description: Each entity changed after `after`, in its latest state, ordered by revision, then `entity_type`, then `entity_id`. `after=0` is a full download and lists only active entities; `after>0` includes deletes (`state: deleted`, `document: null`), and a client ignores a delete for something it doesn't have. A page adds whole revisions until it holds at least `limit` changes, so a revision (a command and its cascades) is never split and a page can exceed `limit`. When more remain, `has_more` is true and `next_after` is the page's last revision; otherwise `next_after` is `head_revision`. An `after` above `head_revision` gets an empty page with `next_after = head_revision`. Each page is read from one consistent snapshot. Clients store `next_after` together with the changes, in one transaction. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return changes after this revision: a decimal integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (STYLE §5), normally the last `next_after`. Default 0 (full download). Anything else is `400 malformed_request`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 200, maximum 500. Anything outside is `400 malformed_request`.

translation.en: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him.

post.summary: Reserve an upload and get a signed PUT link
post.description:
Checks the recording against the upload rules and records a pending upload of it. The checks run in this order, and the first failure answers (contracts/audio/v1/fixtures/audio_upload_validity.json): `content_type` exactly `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp4` (else `415 unsupported_audio_type`); `byte_size` at least 1 (else `422 invalid_size`) and at most 10,000,000 (else `413 file_too_large`); the account's used bytes, ready and pending together, plus `byte_size` at most 500,000,000 (else `422 storage_full`, with `used_bytes` and `limit_bytes`).

The answer is a signed R2 `PUT` link valid for 15 minutes and the headers to send with it. They include `x-amz-checksum-sha256`, so R2 itself refuses bytes that don't match `sha256`. The client then PUTs the file, unchanged, and calls `complete_audio_upload`.

**Idempotent by `asset_id`** (a new UUIDv7 per recording). An `asset_id` the account already has is looked at before the rules: the same body while the upload is pending is `200` with a fresh link (it doesn't count against the quota twice); the same body once the asset is ready is `200 {asset}`, and the client skips the PUT and the completion; a different body, or an ID another account uses, is `409 asset_id_in_use`. `Idempotency-Key` isn't needed: the server accepts the header and ignores it.

A body that breaks the request schema (a non-UUID `asset_id`, `sha256` not 64 lowercase hex digits, a negative `byte_size`, an unknown member) is `400 malformed_request`; clients never send one. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.description: Accepted and ignored; uploads are idempotent by asset_id.

asset_id.description: A new UUIDv7 made by the client. It makes the call idempotent and becomes the asset's ID.

byte_size.description: The file's size in bytes. Wider than the 1 to 10,000,000 an asset may have, so a size the rules refuse gets `invalid_size` or `file_too_large` instead of a 400.

content_type.description: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp4`, exactly. Any other string is `415 unsupported_audio_type`, not a 400.

200.description: A repeat of an earlier request with the same body: while the upload is pending, the same shape as `201` with a fresh link; once the asset is ready, `{asset}`, as `complete_audio_upload` returns it.

201.description: A new pending upload, and its signed PUT link.

409.description: `asset_id_in_use`: the account already used this `asset_id` with a different body, or another account uses it; make a new ID. `account_mismatch`: X-Awrad-Account isn't the signed-in account; nothing was recorded.

value.title: Asset ID in use
value.detail: asset_id was already used for a different file

value.title: Account mismatch
value.detail: X-Awrad-Account is not the signed-in account

413.description: `file_too_large`: `byte_size` is above 10,000,000. The recording stays on the phone.

example.title: File too large
example.detail: byte_size 11534336 is above the 10000000-byte limit

example.title: Unsupported audio type
example.detail: content_type audio/wav is not audio/mpeg or audio/mp4

422.description: `storage_full`: the account's used bytes plus `byte_size` would pass its limit. The problem carries `used_bytes` and `limit_bytes`, for "120 MB of 500 MB"-style messages. `invalid_size`: `byte_size` is 0.

allOf.description: Extension members, present exactly when `code` is `storage_full`.

used_bytes.description: Bytes the account holds now, ready and pending uploads together.

value.title: Storage full
value.detail: 4182733 more bytes would pass the account's 500000000-byte limit

post.summary: Confirm an upload once the file is in storage
post.description:
No request body. The server looks up the stored object and compares its size, content type and SHA-256 with the upload's (it doesn't decode audio). If they match, the upload becomes a ready asset, which a custom dhikr document may now name: `200 {asset}`. Completing a ready asset again returns it again.

- No object yet (the PUT hasn't finished, or failed): `409 upload_incomplete`. PUT again (asking
  `create_audio_upload` for a fresh link if this one expired), then complete again.

- An object that doesn't match: the server deletes the object and the pending upload, and answers
  `422 upload_mismatch`. The recording stays local; a retry starts over with a new `asset_id`.

- An unknown `asset_id`, another account's, one already cleaned up, or not a UUID: `404`.

`Idempotency-Key` is accepted and ignored: completing is idempotent. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

parameters.description: Accepted and ignored; completing is idempotent.

409.description: `upload_incomplete`: storage has no object for this upload yet. `account_mismatch`: X-Awrad-Account isn't the signed-in account; nothing was read or changed.

value.title: Upload incomplete
value.detail: no object has been uploaded for this asset yet

value.title: Account mismatch
value.detail: X-Awrad-Account is not the signed-in account

422.description: `upload_mismatch`: the stored object's size, content type or checksum isn't the upload's. The server has deleted the object and the pending upload.

example.title: Upload mismatch
example.detail: the stored object is 4182000 bytes, not 4182733

get.description: `used_bytes` counts ready assets and pending uploads by their declared `byte_size`; `limit_bytes` is the account's limit (500,000,000). Settings shows it on phones and the web ("120 MB of 500 MB"), and clients may pre-check an upload with it (audio_upload_validity.json). Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.summary: Get a signed link to play or download a recording
get.description: A signed R2 `GET` link to one of the account's ready assets, valid for 10 minutes. Ask for a new one each time playback starts rather than storing it. Phones download the file once into the active profile and play it from there afterwards, offline too; the web plays from the link. An unknown `asset_id`, a pending upload, another account's asset, one already cleaned up, or not a UUID is `404`. Responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.

url.description: Signed R2 GET link, valid until `expires_at`. Treat it as opaque.

bearerAuth.description: Mobile clients. Short-lived access token bound to a device session (ADR-2026-07-12).

cookieAuth.name: _awrad_session
cookieAuth.description: Browser clients. Phoenix session cookie: httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax (ADR-2026-10-15). The cookie name is a placeholder until the server scaffold fixes it.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description: Required with cookieAuth on every state-changing request. Fetch it from `get_browser_csrf_token`.

Uuid.description: Lowercase, hyphenated UUID, any version except nil and max. New IDs are UUIDv7, client-generated for user-owned entities (STYLE §4).

Instant.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Field names end in `_at`.

LocalDate.description: Calendar day `YYYY-MM-DD`. Field names end in `_date`; practice days use `local_date`.

LocalTime.description: Local time of day, 24-hour `HH:MM`. Field names end in `_time`.

CountDelta.description: A signed whole-number change to a count, for example -3 to undo three taps.

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Clients must not parse or build it.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details (STYLE §7). Clients switch on `code` only.

title.description: English, for logs. Never shown to users.

code.description: Stable machine code. Clients map it to localized text.

detail.description: English, for logs. Never shown to users.

errors.description: Field validation errors. Empty when the problem isn't about specific fields.

Email.description: An email address, trimmed by the client (contracts/account-model/v1 email_input). Compared case-insensitively. Invalid ones are `validation_failed` with field code `email_invalid`.

Password.description: 12 to 128 Unicode code points after NFC normalisation, no composition rules (contracts/account-model/v1 password_policy). The server also rejects common passwords. Failures are `validation_failed` with field code `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common`.

EmailCode.description: A 6-digit emailed code, ASCII digits only. Clients normalise what the user typed first (contracts/account-model/v1 email_code_input). Valid for 15 minutes and 5 tries. A malformed code is `validation_failed` with field code `code_invalid`; clients never send one.

Account.description: A signed-in account. Its email is always verified (verification-first).

CurrentPassword.description: The account's current password, re-entered to confirm a sensitive change. A wrong one is `validation_failed` with field code `current_password_incorrect`.

AccountSession.description: One place the account is signed in.

id.description: For a device session, the same `id` as `DeviceSession.id` in its sign-in grant.

name.description: Device model for a device session ("Pixel 9"); a browser and system summary for a browser session ("Firefox on Windows"), or null when it couldn't be told. Clients show a generic label for null.

is_current.description: True for the session making this request.

DeviceInfo.description: Invalid values are `validation_failed` with field codes `installation_id_invalid`, `device_name_invalid` or `platform_invalid` under `/device/...`.

installation_id.description: Random UUID the app creates once per installation and keeps in secure storage (UUIDv7 since ADR-2026-10-28).

name.description: The device model, for example "Pixel 9" or "iPhone 16". Shown in the device list.

idle_expires_at.description: Ends after 30 days without a refresh; each refresh moves it.

absolute_expires_at.description: Ends 180 days after sign-in, whatever happens.

access_token.description: Bearer token, valid for 15 minutes. Keep it in memory only.

refresh_token.description: Single use. Keep it in secure storage (Android Keystore, iOS Keychain).

field.description: JSON Pointer into the request body, for example `/daily_target`.

SyncEntityType.description: What a sync entity is (contracts/sync/v1/README.md). practice_policy and goal_order are one per account, with the account ID as their entity_id; a goal has a new UUIDv7.

SyncVersion.description: Per-entity version. 0 means the entity doesn't exist yet; every applied change adds one.

SyncOptionalTitleText.description: Non-blank text of at most 120 code points, or null.

SyncOptionalLongText.description: Non-blank text of at most 5,000 code points, or null.

CustomDhikrDocument.description: A user's own dhikr (sync.schema.json `custom_dhikr_document`): the catalog dhikr shape without id (the entity_id is the ID), key, aliases, virtues or catalog tags. Lengths are Unicode code points. Invalid ones are rejected per command (custom_dhikr_validity.json).

title.description: Every key present, null when not given (STYLE §3); at least one is text.

audio.description: null (no recording), `{"local_only": true}` (a recording kept only on the device that imported it), or an uploaded recording (slice 3c). Any other shape is a field error `invalid` on /audio.

items.description: A reference exactly as in contracts/dhikr-catalog/v1 `$defs/reference`: `quran` (surah, ayah_start, ayah_end), `hadith`, `book`, `shaykh` or `other`, each with an `id`. Not restated here; the catalog schema is the single definition.

UserTagDocument.description: A user's tag. `name` is trimmed, collapsed and NFC, with 1-40 graphemes and at most 128 UTF-8 bytes; `normalized_name` is its case fold (tag_name_normalization.json). The server recomputes it.

DhikrPersonalDocument.description: A user's own data about one dhikr; its entity_id is the dhikr's ID, built-in or custom. Clients clear tags with an empty list and never delete it.

PracticePolicyDocument.description: The account practice policy (practice-settings.schema.json `practice_policy_document`, slice 3d). Device context (time zone, location) is never part of it. Corrections must also be one per month and keep every month 29 or 30 days (practice_policy_validity.json).

items.description: Moves a Hijri month's start, and every later month's until the next correction.

GoalDocument.description: A goal (goal-model.schema.json `goal_document`, slice 4): its dhikr and a snapshot of the dhikr's label, its name, shared or dedicated counts, dated versions of its settings, pauses, excused days and how it ended. The server also checks the goal rules (goal-model/v1 goal_validity) and that the dhikr is built-in or a custom dhikr of the account.

dhikr_snapshot.description: The dhikr's label when the goal was last saved, so History reads after a custom dhikr is gone.

title.description: Every key present, null when not given (STYLE §3); at least one is text.

counts.description: Which count-log entries fill the goal; set at creation.

versions.description: Dated versions, oldest first; the first starts on created_on.

items.description: A dated version exactly as in contracts/goal-model/v1 `$defs/version`: `from` plus schedule, active_period, count_policy, sessions, requirement, completion and make_up. Not restated here; the goal model schema is the single definition.

GoalOrderDocument.description: The user's order of My Goals (goal-model.schema.json `goal_order_document`, slice 4). One per account, with the account ID as its entity_id. The server drops IDs that aren't a non-deleted goal of the account.

SyncDocument.description: The entity's whole document; which one depends on entity_type.

SyncCommand.description: One change. `put` creates (base_version 0) or replaces the whole document; `delete` makes a final tombstone. command_id is a new UUIDv7 per command.

SyncCurrent.description: The server's copy of a command's entity. document is null when deleted.

field.description: JSON Pointer into the command, for example /document/title/en.

code.description: `range`: a value is out of order with another, such as a Qur'an reference whose ayah_end is below its ayah_start (reported on ayah_end). `immutable`: a goal's dhikr_id or counts differs from the stored goal's.

SyncCascadedChange.description: An entity the server changed as a cascade of the receipt's command, at the same revision: a dhikr_personal a user_tag delete removed the tag from (active); or, for a deleted custom_dhikr, its dhikr_personal (deleted) and each of its goals that had not ended, now ended with reason dhikr_deleted (active).

cascaded.description: An array exactly when the command is a user_tag or custom_dhikr delete: every other entity the server changed at the same revision, ordered by entity_type, then entity_id, and empty when nothing cascaded. Phones set those entities' known versions from it straight away, so the next edit doesn't conflict. null for every other command.

current.description: The server's copy to undo to, or null when it has none.

SyncChange.description: An entity's latest state. document is null when deleted.

AudioContentType.description: The recording's media type, exactly as written: MP3 is `audio/mpeg`, M4A/AAC is `audio/mp4`. Lowercase, no parameters (audio.schema.json `content_type`).

AudioByteSize.description: File size in bytes, 1 to 10,000,000 (10 MB, decimal).

AudioDurationMs.description: Length in milliseconds as the importing client measured it, or null. The server never decodes audio.

Sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

UploadedAudio.description: A recording uploaded to the account's private storage (sync.schema.json `uploaded_audio`). Every member is present. A put naming an `asset_id` that isn't a ready asset of the account is `rejected` with `audio_not_found`; one whose `byte_size` or `content_type` differs from the asset's is `rejected` with `audio_mismatch`.

AudioAsset.description: A confirmed recording of the account (audio.schema.json `asset`). A pending upload isn't an asset.

AudioUpload.description: A pending upload's signed PUT link (audio.schema.json `upload`).

upload_url.description: Signed R2 PUT link, valid until `expires_at` (15 minutes). Treat it as opaque.

upload_headers.description: Headers to send, verbatim and all of them, with the PUT: lowercase header names to values. Today `content-type` (the upload's content_type) and `x-amz-checksum-sha256` (the base64 SHA-256 the link is signed with, so R2 refuses any other bytes). Clients pass the map through rather than building it.

AwradAccount.name: X-Awrad-Account
AwradAccount.description: The account this request's data belongs to: on a phone, the active local profile's account; on the web, the signed-in account. If it isn't the authenticated account, the request is refused with `409 account_mismatch` and nothing is read or written. Missing or not a UUID is `400 malformed_request`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A UUID (clients generate UUIDv7). Replays the stored result for 24 hours (STYLE §10). Clients send it on every retryable POST.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Language for any email this request sends: `en`, `ar` or `ml` (the first supported one wins; default `en`). Clients send the app's current language.

RequiredIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
RequiredIdempotencyKey.description: A UUID (clients generate UUIDv7), required on this operation. A retry with the same key gets the same result.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Each list operation documents its own default and maximum.

RequestId.description: Correlates the request in server logs. Include it in bug reports.

CodeSent.description: Accepted. If the email qualifies, a code is on its way. The response is the same either way, so it doesn't reveal whether the email has an account. Clients offer "send a new code" 60 seconds after this response; a `429` with `Retry-After` overrides that.

DeviceSessionGranted.description: The device session and its tokens.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request, wrong types, or unknown fields.

example.title: Malformed request
example.detail: unknown field "daily_targett"

Unauthorized.description: Not authenticated, credential expired, or the wrong scheme for this pipeline.

example.title: Authentication required
example.detail: no valid session

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed, including an unverified email.

example.title: Email verification required
example.detail: verify the account email first

NotFound.description: Doesn't exist, or isn't visible to this caller. Doesn't say which.

example.title: Not found
example.detail: no such resource

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: email is not a valid address

InvalidCredentials.description: Wrong email or password. Doesn't say which.

example.title: Invalid credentials
example.detail: wrong email or password

CsrfTokenInvalid.description: The CSRF token is missing or doesn't match the session.

example.title: CSRF token invalid
example.detail: missing or stale X-CSRF-Token

VerificationCodeInvalid.description: `verification_code_invalid` (wrong, expired or used code, or unknown email), or `validation_failed` for a malformed email or code.

example.title: Verification code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: password must be at least 12 characters

CurrentPasswordRejected.description: `validation_failed`. Field codes: `current_password_incorrect` on `/current_password`; on operations that take a new password, also `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common` on `/new_password`.

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: the current password is incorrect

AccountMismatch.description: `account_mismatch`: X-Awrad-Account names a different account from the one signed in. Nothing was read or written. A phone stops syncing that profile until the right account signs in.

example.title: Account mismatch
example.detail: X-Awrad-Account is not the signed-in account
